You are given a capacitated facility location optimization problem.

Problem description:
There is a set of candidate facilities, each with a fixed opening cost and a limited service capacity.
There is also a set of customers, each with a known demand.
Serving a customer from a facility incurs a connection cost.

Decision variables:
- Decide which facilities to open.
- Assign each customer to exactly one opened facility.

Constraints:
- Each customer must be assigned to exactly one opened facility.
- A customer can only be assigned to a facility that is opened.
- For every facility, the total demand of assigned customers must not exceed its capacity.

Objective:
Minimize the total cost, defined as the sum of facility opening costs and customer-to-facility connection costs.

You will receive the problem instance in the following format:
{{INSTANCE_INPUT}}

Return your decision in **exactly** this JSON format:
```json
{
  "solution": {
    "selected": [<location_to_open>, <location_to_open>, ...],
    "assignments": [<chosen_open_location>, <chosen_open_location>, ...]
  }
}
```
**Do not include explanations or any extra keys.**

No station can be given more than it can deal with, and every block must be assigned to exactly one open station. As the city waste coordinator, choose which transfer stations to put into operation and decide for every block which active station will collect its refuse, ensuring no station is tasked beyond its handling limit and keeping the combined cost of opening stations and hauling to them as low as possible.

As the retail distribution planner, pick which regional depots to activate and allocate each store’s orders to a single active depot so that no depot’s handling capacity is exceeded and the sum of depot activation fees plus delivery charges is minimized.

As the school lunch program manager, determine which kitchens to staff and assign each school to be supplied by a single staffed kitchen without breaking any kitchen’s production limit while minimizing the total of staffing costs and food transport expenses.

As the hospital network director, decide which outpatient clinics to run and attach every patient population to a single running clinic so that clinic patient limits are respected and the total cost of opening clinics together with patient travel costs is kept as small as possible.

As the festival organizer, select which food stalls to set up and direct each vendor’s customer area to a single set up stall, making sure no stall exceeds its serving capacity and minimizing the overall cost of stall setup plus serving distance.

As the cloud services administrator, choose which data centers to bring online and map each application’s traffic to a single online center so that no center’s bandwidth cap is breached while minimizing the combined cost of bringing centers online and routing traffic.

As the mobile library coordinator, pick which book vans to operate and link each neighborhood to a single operating van so that no van carries more books than its limit and the total of van deployment costs plus delivery effort is minimized.

As the emergency response planner, decide which supply hubs to establish and assign every relief site to a single established hub so that hub stock limits are not exceeded and the sum of hub setup expenses and shipment costs is minimized.

As the solar installer manager, choose which local service teams to activate and schedule each customer’s installation to a single active team without exceeding any team’s workload capacity, while minimizing activation fees plus travel and service costs.

As the telecom rollout coordinator, determine which cell towers to commission and associate each coverage area with a single commissioned tower so that no tower’s user capacity is surpassed and the total of commissioning costs plus connection penalties is as low as possible.

As the pop up clinic scheduler, decide which vaccination sites to open and assign each neighborhood to a single open site, respecting each site’s daily throughput and minimizing the overall cost of opening sites and transporting patients.

As the catering operations lead, select which kitchen trailers to deploy and commit each event to a single deployed trailer so that no trailer is loaded beyond its capacity and the combined cost of trailer deployment and meal delivery is minimized.

As the bike share planner, decide which docking hubs to activate and tie each commuter zone to a single active hub without exceeding docking capacity, while keeping the total cost of activating hubs plus redistribution effort as small as possible.

As the farmer cooperative organizer, pick which packing facilities to operate and allocate every farm’s produce to a single operating facility so that facility throughput limits are honored and the total of facility opening costs and transport charges is minimized.

As the artisan market coordinator, choose which vendor booths to hire and assign each maker to a single hired booth ensuring no booth’s space limit is surpassed, and minimize the sum of booth rental fees plus setup transfer costs.

As the humanitarian logistics manager, select which staging areas to staff and link each beneficiary community to a single staffed area so that no staging area’s capacity is overloaded and the total expense of staffing plus distribution is minimized.

As the bookstore chain operations manager, decide which local warehouses to activate and route each shop’s restock orders to a single active warehouse while not exceeding any warehouse’s capacity and minimizing the total of warehouse fixed costs and shipping fees.

As the municipal bike repair program lead, choose which repair centers to open and assign every reported fault to a single open center so that center workload limits are respected and the overall sum of opening costs and service travel is minimized.

As the nonprofit food bank coordinator, determine which distribution points to staff and allocate each recipient area to a single staffed point without surpassing any point’s distribution capacity, minimizing combined staffing and delivery costs.

As the electronics return manager, pick which repair hubs to keep operating and direct each returned device to a single operating hub so that no hub’s processing limit is exceeded and the total cost of keeping hubs open and moving devices is minimized.

As the city planner, choose which neighborhood meal centers to activate and assign each household to an activated center without splitting any household across centers, ensure no center serves more demand than its capacity, and keep the combined cost of center activation and meal delivery as low as possible.

As the festival organizer, pick which temporary water stations to set up and send attendees to an established station with no attendee split between stations, respect the serving limits of each station, and minimize the total of setup fees and attendee walking distances.

As the university housing coordinator, decide which dormitory wings to open and allocate students to opened wings without splitting any student across wings, respect bed capacity at every wing, and minimize the sum of opening expenses plus student relocation distance costs.

As a retail logistics manager, select which local pickup lockers to activate and assign customers to activated lockers with no customer split across lockers, ensure each locker does not exceed its parcel capacity, and keep the total of activation charges and customer travel to lockers as low as possible.

As an NGO disaster relief lead, determine which temporary shelters to set up and place affected families into opened shelters without splitting households among shelters, ensure no shelter is assigned more occupants than its capacity, and minimize the overall cost of shelter setup plus transport expenses.

As a telecom operations manager, choose which edge servers to provision and map user devices to provisioned servers without splitting traffic from any device across servers, ensure each server handles no more load than its capacity, and minimize the sum of server provisioning costs and connection latency penalties.

As the farmer market coordinator, decide which vendor stalls to rent and assign sellers to rented stalls without dividing a seller across stalls, respect the space limit for each stall, and keep the total of stall rental expenses and sellers' setup travel as small as possible.

As the campus dining director, choose which satellite kitchens to operate and allocate student groups to operating kitchens without splitting any group, make sure no kitchen is asked to serve beyond its capacity, and minimize the total of kitchen operating costs plus food distribution costs.

connection_item_fields.name: cost

global_fields.name: num_facilities

connection_item_fields.name: cost

facility_item_fields.name: opening_cost

facility_item_fields.name: capacity

connection_item_fields.name: customer_id
